This year could be said to be the inaugural year of super apps. OpenAI recently launched its own super app and openly admitted that the app was "a bit of a mess." Now, the CEO of Microsoft has also confirmed that a Copilot super app will be launched in the near future.

The Microsoft Copilot "super app" will integrate Cowork, chat, and coding functions all in one.

Microsoft is developing an AI "super app" that brings together the chat, coding, and agentic capabilities of Copilot. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said on Wednesday's earnings call that the app will launch within this year and will cover "consumer and business experiences." Nadella noted: "Copilot is rapidly evolving from chat functionality to Cowork, and then to Autopilots. This quarter, we will integrate these Copilot experiences—including coding capabilities—into a single super app… This is a major step forward, and I look forward to sharing more details with you later."

OpenAI's process of launching its own "super app" was nothing short of chaotic, but that has clearly not deterred other companies from continuing to follow the super app route.

Perhaps Microsoft will be able to deliver an all-in-one app more successfully and avoid repeating OpenAI's mistakes.

That said, CEO Satya Nadella also recently stated that the company is gradually shifting from apps and focusing its attention on agents. The AI era is still in its early stages, and the trends and best practices for building AI-centric interfaces are still changing rapidly.

As for Apple, there are no signs of a shift toward the super app strategy; instead, the company continues to launch new and specialised standalone apps. Whether it will change course in the future remains to be seen.

What are your views on the recent "super app" boom? Feel free to share with us in the comments section.
